intro: This unit tells the story of Moses. It comes from the book of Exodus. Exodus is the second book of the Bible. The story starts with a baby in a basket. It ends at a big mountain.
You will meet a brave sister, a kind princess and a king who says no. You will read about a bush on fire, walls of water and bread in the desert. Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell this story.
By the end, you will be able to tell the story in order. You will know what Passover is. You will know why this story matters to so many people.
bigQuestion: How does the Exodus story say a people went from slaves to free?

timeline.t: Jacob's family grows into a big people in Egypt
A new Pharaoh makes the Israelites slaves
A mother hides her baby in a basket on the Nile
Pharaoh's daughter finds the baby and names him Moses
Moses grows up, runs away and becomes a shepherd
Moses sees the burning bush and is sent back to Egypt
Pharaoh says no, and the ten plagues come
The night of Passover, and the people leave Egypt
The sea opens and the people cross on dry ground
The Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai

words.d: the second book of the Bible; the word means going out
the name for the king of Egypt
the big family of Jacob, also called Israel; the people in the story
the baby from the basket who grew up to lead the people out of Egypt
the ten hard things the story says came to Egypt
the night the people left Egypt; a holiday Jews keep every spring
the bread-like food the story says the people found in the desert
the ten rules the story says were given at Mount Sinai

test.q: Which book tells the story of Moses?
test.why: Exodus, the second book of the Bible, tells the story of Moses.

test.q: What did the new Pharaoh do to the Israelites?
test.why: Exodus 1 says the new king made the Israelites work as slaves.

test.q: What did the mother put her baby in?
test.why: Exodus 2 says she made a basket of reeds, covered it with tar, and set it in the river.

test.q: Who found the baby in the basket?
test.why: Exodus 2 says Pharaoh's daughter found the basket in the reeds.

test.q: What did Moses see on the mountain in Midian?
choices: A bush on fire that did not burn up
test.why: Exodus 3 says Moses saw a bush burning that was not burned up.

test.q: What message did Moses and Aaron bring to Pharaoh?
test.why: In Exodus 5, they tell Pharaoh, "Let my people go."

test.q: Why is the bread flat at Passover?
choices: The people left in a hurry, so it did not rise
It was baked on the sea
test.why: Exodus 12 says the people left Egypt in a hurry, so the bread had no time to rise.

test.q: How did the story say the people crossed the sea?
choices: On dry ground between walls of water
test.why: Exodus 14 says the sea split and the people walked on dry ground.

test.q: What did the people find on the ground each morning in the desert?
test.why: Exodus 16 says manna, a bread-like food, was on the ground each morning.

test.q: Which is one of the Ten Commandments?
test.why: Do not tell lies about your neighbor is one of the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20.

write.prompt: Was Moses brave? Tell about two parts of the story. Use the basket story in Exodus 2, the bush in Exodus 3, or the sea in Exodus 14. Say what the story says. Then say what you think.
tips: Name the book and chapter, like Exodus 3.
Say the story says, not it really happened.
Use words from the unit, like Pharaoh and plagues.

title: Moses and the Way Out

chapters.title: A Baby in a Basket
chapters.bigQuestion: How does the story say a baby in a basket grew up to be a leader?

story.title: The Basket in the Reeds
story.kicker: A mother makes a little boat, and a big sister watches from the tall grass.
paragraphs: The river was wide and slow. Tall reeds grew along the edge. A mother knelt by the water. She held a basket made of reeds. She had painted it with tar so no water could get in. Inside the basket was her baby boy.
The mother kissed the baby. She set the basket in the reeds. The water rocked it softly. Then she walked away. Her heart was full of worry. She did not know what would happen next.
A girl hid in the tall grass. She was the baby's big sister. She did not move. She did not make a sound. She watched the basket. She waited to see who would come.
This is a story from the book of Exodus. Exodus is the second book of the Bible. Jews and Christians tell this story. Muslims tell a story of this baby too. His name was Moses.
story.think: The big sister stayed to watch the basket. Why do you think she stayed?

lessons.title: Many, Many People
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jacob's family grew into a big people in Egypt.
reading: Remember Joseph? His family moved to *Egypt*. Egypt is a land by a long river. The river is called the Nile. The family had food there.
Years went by. The family grew and grew. The story says they became a big people. They were called the Israelites. That name comes from Jacob. Jacob was also called Israel.
Exodus is the book that tells this. It is the second book of the Bible. The first chapter says the Israelites filled the land.

words.d: a land in Africa by the Nile River, where the story says Jacob's family went to live
the big family of Jacob, who was also called Israel; the people in the Exodus story

look.title: Picture a Family Growing
look.text: Picture one big tent. Inside are Jacob's twelve sons and their children. Now picture many years going by. There are hundreds of tents. Then thousands. Children run between them. A whole town of one family fills the land by the river.
look.prompt: How did one family turn into a whole people? Tell it in your own words.

check.q: Where did Jacob's family live in the Exodus story?
check.why: The story says Jacob's family moved to Egypt in Joseph's time and grew there.

check.q: What book of the Bible tells the story of Moses?
check.why: Exodus is the second book of the Bible. It tells the story of Moses.

check.q: What does the name Israelites come from?
choices: Jacob, who was also called Israel
check.why: Jacob was given the name Israel. His family became the Israelites.

lessons.title: A New King Says Work
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a new king made the Israelites work as slaves.
reading: A new king came to rule Egypt. The king of Egypt was called *Pharaoh*. Pharaoh did not know Joseph. He looked at the Israelites. He saw how many they were. He was afraid.
So Pharaoh made them *slaves*. A slave is a person who is not free. The Israelites had to make bricks. They had to build cities. They worked all day in the hot sun.
The story says Pharaoh made a cruel rule too. It put the Israelite baby boys in danger. Two brave helpers said no to the king. Their names were Shiphrah and Puah.

words.d: the name for the king of Egypt
people who are not free and are made to work for someone else

look.title: The Story Says
look.text: A new king came to rule Egypt. He did not know Joseph. He said the Israelites were too many. So he made them work very hard. They built cities for him. But the more they were pushed down, the more they grew.
look.cite: Exodus 1, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why was the new king afraid of the Israelites?

check.q: What is a Pharaoh?
check.why: In the story, Pharaoh is the name for the king of Egypt.

check.q: What did the Israelites have to do as slaves?
check.why: Exodus 1 says they made bricks and built cities for Pharaoh.

check.q: Who said no to the king's cruel rule?
check.why: Exodus 1 names two helpers, Shiphrah and Puah, who did not obey the king.

lessons.title: A Mother's Plan
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a mother hid her baby in a basket on the river to keep him safe.
reading: A mother had a baby boy. She saw he was a fine baby. She hid him for three months. But a baby cries. She could not hide him forever.
So she made a plan. She made a *basket* out of reeds. She painted it with tar. Now water could not get in. She put the baby inside. She set it in the reeds by the *Nile*.
The baby's sister stood far off. She watched to see what would happen. The story says her name was Miriam.

words.d: a container woven from reeds or straw; in the story it floats like a little boat
the long river that runs through Egypt

look.title: A Basket That Floats
look.text: Look at a basket made of reeds. It has holes between the reeds. Water would leak in. Now look at the same basket painted with black, sticky tar. The holes are filled. Now it floats like a little boat.
look.prompt: Why did the mother paint the basket with tar? What would happen without it?

check.q: How long did the mother hide her baby at home?
check.why: Exodus 2 says she hid him for three months before she made the basket.

check.q: What was the basket made of?
check.why: The story says the basket was made of reeds and covered with tar.

check.q: Who watched the basket from far off?
check.why: Exodus 2 says the baby's sister stood far off to watch.

lessons.title: A Princess Finds a Baby
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Pharaoh's daughter found the baby and named him Moses.
reading: Pharaoh's daughter came to the river. She wanted to wash. She saw the basket in the reeds. She opened it. The baby was crying. She felt sorry for him.
Then the sister ran up. She said, "Shall I find a woman to feed the baby?" The princess said yes. The sister ran and got her own mother! So the baby's mother took care of him.
When he was bigger, he went to live with the princess. She named him *Moses*. The story says the name means "I pulled him out of the water."

words.d: the baby found in the basket; the story says his name means pulled out of the water

look.title: Out of the Water
look.text: Pharaoh's daughter saw the basket in the reeds. She sent a helper to get it. She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying. She felt sorry for him. She said, "This is one of the Hebrew children." Later she named him Moses, because she pulled him out of the water.
look.cite: Exodus 2:5-10, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: The princess knew the baby was an Israelite. She kept him anyway. What does that tell you about her?

check.q: Who found the baby in the basket?
check.why: Exodus 2 says Pharaoh's daughter came to the river and found the basket.

check.q: Who took care of the baby while he was little?
check.why: The sister brought the baby's own mother, and the princess let her care for him.

check.q: What does the story say the name Moses means?
check.why: Exodus 2:10 says the princess named him Moses because she pulled him out of the water.

lessons.title: Moses Runs Away
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses grew up, got in trouble, and ran away to a far land.
reading: Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house. But he knew he was an Israelite. One day he saw a man hitting an Israelite slave. Moses got very angry. He hit the man hard, and the man died.
Pharaoh heard about it. He wanted to punish Moses. So Moses ran away. He went to a far land called *Midian*.
In Midian, Moses sat by a well. He helped some sisters get water for their sheep. Their father was glad. Moses married one sister. Her name was Zipporah. Moses became a *shepherd*.

words.d: the far land where the story says Moses lived after he ran away from Egypt
a person who takes care of sheep

look.title: From a Palace to a Field
look.text: Picture Moses in Pharaoh's house. He has nice clothes and lots of food. Now picture Moses in Midian. He walks in the dust all day with sheep. He sleeps in a tent. His life is very different now.
look.prompt: How was Moses's life in Midian different from his life in Egypt?

check.q: Why did Moses run away from Egypt?
choices: He wanted to see the sea
He got in trouble with Pharaoh
check.why: Exodus 2 says Moses hurt a man, and Pharaoh wanted to punish him, so he ran.

check.q: Where did Moses go when he ran away?
check.why: The story says Moses went to the land of Midian.

check.q: What job did Moses do in Midian?
check.why: Exodus 3 says Moses kept the sheep of his wife's father.

lessons.title: The Bush That Kept Burning
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses saw a bush on fire that did not burn up, and heard God speak.
reading: One day Moses led the sheep to a mountain. He saw a bush on fire. But the bush did not burn up! Moses went closer to look.
The story says God spoke to Moses from the bush. God said, "Take off your shoes. This is *holy* ground." Holy means set apart and special.
Then the story says God told Moses a job. "My people are hurting in Egypt. Go to Pharaoh. Bring my people out." Moses was scared. He said, "Who am I to do this?"

words.d: set apart as special; in the story, the ground near the bush was holy

look.title: Holy Ground
look.text: Moses saw a bush burning with fire. But the bush was not burned up. He said, "I will go and see this strange thing." Then the story says God called to him from the bush: "Moses, Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am."
look.cite: Exodus 3:2-4, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What did Moses see that was strange? What did he say when God called his name?

check.q: What was strange about the bush?
choices: It was on fire but did not burn up
check.why: Exodus 3 says the bush burned with fire but was not burned up.

check.q: What does holy mean?
check.why: Holy means set apart as special. God told Moses the ground was holy.

check.q: What job did the story say God gave Moses?
choices: Go to Pharaoh and bring the people out
check.why: In Exodus 3, God sends Moses to Pharaoh to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.

lessons.title: Let My People Go
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses went back to Egypt to tell Pharaoh to let the people go.
reading: Moses did not feel brave. He said, "I am not good at talking." The story says God gave him a helper. It was his brother, *Aaron*. Aaron could speak well.
So Moses went back to Egypt. He was old now. Aaron went with him. They stood in front of Pharaoh. They gave him a *message*. A message is words you carry for someone else.
The message was short. "Let my people go." Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell this part. The Qur'an calls Moses by the name Musa.

words.d: Moses's brother, who spoke for him in the story
words you carry to someone from someone else

look.title: The Message to Pharaoh
look.text: Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
look.prompt: Who is the message from, and who carried it? Say it in your own words.

check.q: Who helped Moses talk to Pharaoh?
check.why: Exodus 4 says Aaron would speak for Moses because Moses said he was not good at talking.

check.q: What was the message to Pharaoh?
check.why: In Exodus 5, Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh, "Let my people go."

check.q: What name does the Qur'an use for Moses?
check.why: The Qur'an tells the story of Moses too, and calls him Musa.

review.q: Which book of the Bible tells the story of Moses?
review.why: Exodus, the second book of the Bible, tells the story of Moses.

review.q: Why did Pharaoh make the Israelites slaves?
choices: He saw how many they were and was afraid
review.why: Exodus 1 says the new king was afraid because the Israelites were so many.

review.q: Where did the mother put the basket?
choices: In the reeds by the Nile
review.why: Exodus 2 says she set the basket in the reeds by the river.

review.q: Who watched from far off to see what would happen?
review.why: The baby's sister, later called Miriam, watched from far off.

review.q: Where did the story say God spoke to Moses?
review.why: Exodus 3 says God spoke to Moses from a bush that burned but did not burn up.

review.q: What did Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh?
review.why: In Exodus 5, they carry the message, "Let my people go."

chapters.title: Through the Sea to a Mountain
chapters.bigQuestion: How does the story say the people got out of Egypt and what did they get at the mountain?

story.title: Dry Ground in the Middle
story.kicker: Water stands up on both sides, and a whole people walks through.
paragraphs: The people stood at the edge of the sea. Behind them came Pharaoh's army. Horses. Chariots. Dust in the air. The people were scared. There was nowhere to go.

The story says Moses held out his hand over the water. A strong wind blew all night. The sea moved apart. On the left was a wall of water. On the right was a wall of water. In the middle was dry ground.
The people walked through. Mothers held babies. Children held hands. Old people leaned on sticks. The walls of water stood tall on both sides. The bottom of the sea was under their feet.
This is the story of the Exodus. Exodus means going out. Jews remember it every year at Passover. Christians read it too. Let's read it from the beginning.
story.think: What would you see, hear and feel walking between two walls of water?

lessons.title: Ten Hard Things
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Pharaoh said no, so ten hard things called plagues came to Egypt.
reading: Moses said, "Let my people go." Pharaoh said no. He said it again and again. The story says hard things came to Egypt. They are called *plagues*.
First the river turned red like blood. Then frogs came everywhere. Then tiny bugs. Then flies. The animals got sick. People got sores. Hail fell. Locusts ate the plants. It got dark for three days.
Nine times Pharaoh said no. The tenth plague was the saddest of all. Then Pharaoh finally said, "Go."

words.d: the ten hard things the story says came to Egypt when Pharaoh said no

look.title: The Plagues in Order
look.prompt: Which plague came first? Which came last on this list?

check.q: What are the plagues in the story?
choices: Ten hard things that came to Egypt
check.why: The plagues are the ten hard things Exodus says came to Egypt when Pharaoh said no.

check.q: What happened to the river in the first plague?
check.why: Exodus 7 says the water of the river turned to blood.

check.q: How many times did Pharaoh say no before the last plague?
check.why: Pharaoh said no through nine plagues. After the tenth, he said go.

lessons.title: The Night of Passover
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people ate a special meal in a hurry on the night they left Egypt.
reading: The story says God told the people to get ready. Each family cooked a lamb. They put a mark on their door. They ate bread with no yeast. There was no time to let it rise.
They ate fast. They had their shoes on. They were ready to run. The story says the sad tenth plague passed over their houses. That is why the night is called *Passover*.
That night Pharaoh said go. The people left Egypt. They took their bread dough with them. It was still flat. Flat bread is called *matzah*.

words.d: the night the story says the people left Egypt; a holiday Jews keep every year
flat bread with no yeast, eaten at Passover

look.title: Eat It in a Hurry
look.text: The story says: eat the meal this way. Have your belt on. Have your shoes on your feet. Hold your walking stick in your hand. Eat it in a hurry. It is the Lord's Passover.
look.cite: Exodus 12:11, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why did the people eat with their shoes on and their sticks in their hands?

check.q: Why was the bread flat on Passover night?
choices: There was no time to let it rise
check.why: Exodus 12 says the people left in a hurry, so the bread had no time to rise.

check.q: What is matzah?
check.why: Matzah is the flat bread with no yeast that is eaten at Passover.

check.q: Why is the night called Passover?
choices: The story says the tenth plague passed over their houses
The people passed over a mountain
Pharaoh passed by on a horse
check.why: Exodus 12 says the last plague passed over the marked houses.

lessons.title: The Sea Opens
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the sea opened and the people crossed on dry ground.
reading: The people walked out of Egypt. But Pharaoh changed his mind. He sent his army after them. The people came to the sea. They were trapped.
The story says Moses held his hand over the sea. A strong wind blew all night. The water split in two. The people walked across on dry ground. Water stood like a wall on each side.
Pharaoh's army followed. Then the water came back. The army could not get through. The people were safe. They were free.

words.d: a big group of soldiers; Pharaoh sent his army with horses and chariots
not a slave; able to go where you choose

look.title: A Wall on Each Side
look.text: The story says Moses stretched his hand over the sea. A strong east wind blew all night. The sea became dry land. The Israelites went into the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was a wall for them on their right hand and on their left.
look.cite: Exodus 14:21-22, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Draw or describe what the people saw on their right and on their left.

check.q: Why were the people trapped at the sea?
choices: The army was behind them and the sea in front
It was too dark to see
check.why: Exodus 14 says Pharaoh's army came behind them while the sea was in front.

check.q: What did the story say blew all night?
check.why: Exodus 14 says a strong east wind blew all night and the sea split.

check.q: What did the people walk on when they crossed?
check.why: The story says the people crossed on dry ground with water on both sides.

lessons.title: A Song and Some Bread
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people sang for joy, then found strange bread in the desert.
reading: On the other side, the people sang. Miriam took a small drum. She led the women in a dance. They sang a song of thanks.
Then they walked into the *desert*. A desert is dry land with little water. Soon the people were hungry. They grumbled at Moses.
The story says thin flakes fell on the ground each morning. The people asked, "What is it?" That is what the word *manna* means. They ate it like bread. It tasted like honey cakes.

words.d: dry land with little water and few plants
the bread-like food the story says the people found in the desert; the name asks What is it?

look.title: What Is It?
look.text: Look at the desert ground in the morning. There is dew on the sand. The dew dries up. Small white flakes are left. They look like frost. You pick one up. You taste it. It is sweet like honey.
look.prompt: The people called this food manna. Why do you think they gave it that name?

check.q: Who led the women in a song and dance by the sea?
check.why: Exodus 15 says Miriam took a timbrel, a small drum, and led the women.

check.q: What is a desert?
check.why: A desert is dry land with little water and few plants.

check.q: What does the word manna mean?
check.why: Exodus 16 says the people asked what it was. That question became the name manna.

lessons.title: Ten Rules on Stone
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people came to Mount Sinai and were given ten rules.
reading: The people came to a big mountain. It was called *Mount Sinai*. The story says a cloud covered the top. There was thunder. There was a loud horn. The mountain shook.
The story says God gave the people rules. There were ten of them. They are called the *Ten Commandments*. Later they were written on two flat stones.
Here are some in kid words. Tell the truth. Do not steal. Rest one day each week. Be good to your mom and dad. Do not want what belongs to someone else.

words.d: the mountain where the story says the people were given the Ten Commandments
the ten rules the story says were given at Mount Sinai

look.title: Some of the Ten
look.text: The story says these words were spoken at the mountain. Honor your father and your mother. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about your neighbor. Do not want your neighbor's house or anything that is your neighbor's.
look.cite: Exodus 20:12-17, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Pick one rule. Tell what it looks like to keep it at school.

check.q: Where does the story say the ten rules were given?
check.why: Exodus 19 and 20 say the people were at Mount Sinai when the rules were given.

check.q: What are the ten rules called?
check.why: The ten rules from Mount Sinai are called the Ten Commandments.

check.q: Which of these is one of the ten rules?
check.why: Do not steal is one of the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20.

lessons.title: One Day to Rest
lessons.mainIdea: One of the ten rules says to rest one day each week, and the story links it to creation.
reading: One rule is about rest. It says work six days. Then rest on the seventh day. This day is called the *Sabbath*.
Remember the very first story? Genesis says God made the world in six days. Then God rested on the seventh day. The rule at Sinai points back to that story.
Many Jews rest on Saturday. That is their Sabbath. Many Christians rest and go to church on Sunday. Both get the idea of a rest day from this story.

words.d: the day of rest, one day in every seven

look.title: Numbers at the Mountain
rows: Stones the rules were written on
look.cite: Exodus 20 and Exodus 31:18, King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: How many days of work come before the day of rest?

check.q: What is the Sabbath?
choices: A day to cross the sea
check.why: The Sabbath is the day of rest, one day in every seven.

check.q: What story does the rest rule point back to?
check.why: Exodus 20 links the rest day to God resting on the seventh day in Genesis.

check.q: On which day do many Jews keep the Sabbath?
check.why: Many Jews rest on Saturday, their Sabbath. Many Christians rest on Sunday.

lessons.title: Remembering Every Year
lessons.mainIdea: Jews remember the Exodus every year at Passover, and Christians read the story too.
reading: Every spring, Jewish families have a special meal. It is called a *Seder*. They eat matzah. They tell the Exodus story. The youngest child asks questions.
The story tells families to do this. It says, "When your children ask, tell them." So the story is told again every year.
Christians read the Exodus story too. The Gospels say Jesus ate a Passover meal with his friends. Muslims tell the story of Musa and the sea. One story, many tellers.

words.d: the special Passover meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story

look.title: At the Seder Table
look.text: Picture a long table. There is a plate with flat matzah. There are bitter herbs. There is a cup of grape juice. A little girl stands up. She asks, "Why is this night different from all other nights?" Her grandpa smiles and begins the story.
look.prompt: Why do you think families tell the same story every year?

check.q: What is a Seder?
choices: A Passover meal where the story is told
check.why: A Seder is the special meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story.

check.q: Who asks the questions at the Seder?
check.why: At the Seder, the youngest child asks the questions, and the story is the answer.

check.q: What does the story tell families to do when children ask?
check.why: Exodus 12 and 13 say to tell the children what happened when they ask.

review.q: What is a plague in this story?
choices: A hard thing that came to Egypt
review.why: The plagues were the ten hard things Exodus says came to Egypt.

review.q: What did the people eat on Passover night?
review.why: Exodus 12 says each family ate a lamb and bread with no yeast.

review.q: What stood on both sides when the people crossed the sea?
review.why: Exodus 14 says the water was a wall on their right and on their left.

choices: Food the story says fell in the desert
review.why: Exodus 16 says manna was the bread-like food the people found each morning.

review.q: What did the story say was given at Mount Sinai?
review.why: Exodus 20 tells of the Ten Commandments given at Mount Sinai.

review.q: When do Jews remember the Exodus every year?
review.why: Jewish families remember the Exodus at the Passover Seder every spring.
